seo_description: Kids' Christmas in Forney, TX: Bell Park Tree Lighting, Christmas on Main, Pictures with Santa and Mrs. Claus at The OC, and the Candy Cane Hunt.
lede: The story of Christmas in Forney begins with a railroad, when residents renamed their community Forney on December 29, 1873, after a Texas and Pacific Railway board member, John Wien Forney. Today the season opens with the Bell Park Tree Lighting in Downtown Forney, followed by Christmas on Main, Pictures with Santa and Mrs. Claus at The OC and a Flashlight Candy Cane Hunt.
sections: Bell Park Tree Lighting and Christmas on Main

The City of Forney lights its community Christmas tree at the annual Bell Park Tree Lighting Ceremony on Thursday, December 3, 2026, from 6 to 8 pm in Downtown Forney, with Christmas music, Santa and free hot chocolate. Two days later, on Saturday, December 5, Christmas on Main fills downtown from noon to 5 pm with holiday vendors, crafts and activities. The city's event page says Christmas on Main is its yearly celebration of the holiday season in Downtown Forney.
Pictures with Santa and a Flashlight Candy Cane Hunt

The OC, run by Forney ISD at 680 Innovation Boulevard, hosts free Pictures with Santa and Mrs. Claus in its Green Room on the west side, from November 28 to December 20, 2026. Hours are Fridays 6 to 8 pm, Saturdays 10 am to 4 pm and Sundays 1 to 4 pm, and opening weekend is Saturday, November 28, 10 am to 4 pm, and Sunday, November 29, 1 to 4 pm. On Tuesday, December 15, Forney Parks and Recreation holds the free Flashlight Candy Cane Hunt at Forney Community Park, 241 S FM 548, starting at 6:15 pm, and the city asks families to arrive on time.
A town renamed for the railroad

The Handbook of Texas says settlers called the town Brooklyn in 1870. When the Texas and Pacific Railway promoters built through the settlement in 1873 and the community applied for a post office, residents renamed it Forney on December 29, 1873, honoring the railroad, the federal post office approval and John Wien Forney, a Pennsylvania journalist, politician and railway board member. Forney was incorporated in 1884 and had more than 3,000 residents by 1960. For trains today, the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano, the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco and the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley in Dallas all have Rally pages.

faq: How did Forney get its name?

The Handbook of Texas says settlers called the town Brooklyn in 1870. When the Texas and Pacific Railway built through in 1873, residents renamed it Forney on December 29, 1873, honoring the railroad, the post office approval and John Wien Forney, a Pennsylvania journalist, politician and railway board member.

Forney was incorporated in 1884, according to the Handbook of Texas, about a decade after the Texas and Pacific Railway promoters built through the settlement in 1873. The same source says the town had more than 3,000 residents by 1960.
